text:
ryan_support: Customer ScribeAI reporting repeated 503s for /v1/generate since ~09:12 UTC. Customer sees timeouts and occasional 500 with "upstream unavailable". They say it started right after a model switch.

jamie_sre: Oncall - I'm seeing a restart spike on hosted-runner-ml-* between 09:10-09:14. restartCount went from 0 -> 4 for a subset. Correlates with increased GPU mem and OOMs. Pulling logs now. :eyes:

ryan_support: customer provided trace_id=tre-9b3f4, requests show 503 gateway errors and then retries. They also flagged billing duplicates for retried requests (customer unhappy).

marta_eng: quick scan of recent deploys: model-router rolled out model v2.2-quantized at 08:52 (traffic shift), serving runtime image unchanged. Suspect the quantized kernel path plus kv-prefetch/resize interplay.

deploybot: Deploy bot: rollout model-router@2026-03-16T08:52 (canary -> 100%). No infra changes.

ryan_support: attaching runner excerpt (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-16T09:12:10Z] runner[pid=1842] ERROR UpstreamWorker: segfault (SIGSEGV) at 0x7f3a2c4b8d
  #0  0x7f3a2c4b8d in attention_forward(libattention.so)
  #1  0x7f3a1f8a22 in kv_prefetch
  #2  0x55b3c7b4a in run_inference
  GPU memory before crash: 101.2%
  OOM events logged by nvidia-smi around the same time.
```

jamie_sre: repro steps I'm doing:
1) hit /v1/generate with long context (8k tokens) and batch factor 4
2) observe kv-cache prefetch spike in mem and then segfault after ~10s

Commands I'm running:
```bash
kubectl -n hosted logs runner-abc --since=20m | grep -i segfault
kubectl -n hosted describe pod runner-abc | egrep "Restart|OOM"
nvidia-smi dmon -s u -d 1
```

marta_eng: temporary mitigation options:
- disable kv-prefetch for quantized models: set REDWOOD_PREFETCH_ENABLED=false in runtime config for affected pool
- rollback traffic to model v2.1.4 (non-quantized)
- pin customer to Dedicated fallback routing until hotfix

ryan_support: customer wants a fast fix. Can we pin ScribeAI to previous model version and enable fallback routing? Also need accounting check for duplicate billing on retried 503s (billing team loop).

jamie_sre: I can shift the router rule for that customer to fallback pool (no GPU) in ~5m. Doing now: `routerctl route set --customer scribeai --pool fallback-cpu`

opsbot: Incident INC-2026-0316-0921 created by jamie_sre. Priority: P1. Paging oncall.

carol_cs: Notified ScribeAI PM and apologized; asked for trace_ids and timestamp window (09:10-09:15). They want ETA for fix.

marta_eng: creating hotfix branch to guard kv-prefetch when model.quantized==true and observed ctx_len>4096. Draft PR #4456, will push a patch to runtime in ~30-60m and coordinate a safe rollout without full model rollback.

jamie_sre: short-term actions executed:
- router pinned ScribeAI to fallback-cpu pool (effective 09:19)
- scaled down affected runner pool to 0 and cordoned nodes
- collecting core dumps + gdb bt on segfaulting binary; saved to upload bucket (s3://redwood-incident-3361234567/)

ryan_support: customer confirmed traffic routed to fallback pool and errors reduced to 0 on their end. They're still worried about billing duplicates, I've opened ticket BILL-789 for billing ops.

marta_eng: will monitor post-patch and follow up with roll-forward plan. ETA for patch bake: 45m, then progressive rollout. If patch not safe, fallback is to rollback model traffic to v2.1.4.

jamie_sre: next steps for SRE: collect heap profiles, nvml logs, and exact pod env for reproducer. I'll keep this thread updated.

ryan_support: thanks all. tagging @billing-ops and @cust-suc for follow-up. :thumbsup:
